Softline, the women’s apparel brand from Rupa & Company Limited, has introduced a refreshed brand identity as it looks to strengthen its appeal among a new generation of consumers while building on its longstanding presence in the market.

The rebranding is accompanied by updated product collections across lingerie, athleisure and outerwear, reflecting the brand’s evolving design direction. Through a modern visual approach, Softline aims to enhance its relevance in the women’s apparel segment while retaining the trust it has established over the years.

Drawing inspiration from themes of freshness, femininity and everyday style, the new identity incorporates floral elements, vibrant colour palettes and contemporary design aesthetics across its collections. The updated visual language is intended to create a stronger retail presence and a more cohesive brand experience.

The latest range includes bras, camisoles, panties, leggings and pants, designed to cater to women navigating different aspects of daily life, from work and travel to fitness and leisure. The collections focus on combining comfort and functionality with contemporary styling, enabling consumers to adapt their wardrobe to a variety of occasions.

As part of this new chapter, Softline has partnered with actor Wamiqa Gabbi as the face of the brand. Known for her work in film and digital entertainment, Gabbi’s personal style and on-screen presence align with the values the brand seeks to communicate through its refreshed positioning.

Wamiqa’s individuality, versatility, and effortless approach to fashion make her a strong representative of the brand’s evolving identity. Her preference for clothing that balances style, comfort and practicality reflects the design philosophy behind Softline’s latest collections.

The revamped brand positioning emphasizes fashion that fits naturally into everyday life while encouraging self-expression. Softline’s updated identity is built around the idea that comfort and confidence can coexist, allowing consumers to wear fashion in a way that reflects their personal preferences and lifestyles.

The company said the refreshed collections are designed to support women across a range of activities and occasions, from casual everyday dressing to more statement-led fashion choices, while maintaining a focus on fit, quality and ease of wear.

With its refreshed identity, updated product portfolio and new brand ambassador, Softline is aiming to strengthen its position in India’s women’s apparel market and connect with a broader base of fashion-conscious consumers seeking comfort-driven, versatile wardrobe solutions.

Eyewear brand Ray-Ban and smart glasses platform Ray-Ban Meta have appointed actor Ranveer Singh as their first-ever brand ambassador for the Indian market, marking a new phase in the brand’s presence in the country.

The partnership builds on Ranveer’s previous collaborations with Meta and aims to combine Ray-Ban’s heritage of self-expression with Meta’s AI-powered technology. Through the association, the brands seek to highlight how iconic eyewear styles and smart technology can come together to create new consumer experiences.

As part of the collaboration, Ranveer will feature in campaigns for both Ray-Ban and Ray-Ban Meta, bringing his personal style and creative perspective to the brands’ storytelling efforts in India. The partnership also reflects the increasing focus on wearable technology and AI-powered consumer products within the lifestyle and fashion segment.

Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses are designed to offer hands-free functionality, enabling users to listen to music and podcasts, make calls, and access Meta AI features without relying on a smartphone. The product continues to evolve through software updates and the addition of new AI capabilities and connected experiences.

Ranveer Singh said, “Ray-Ban has always stood for individuality, and that is something I have connected with for as long as I can remember. Style, for me, has never been about following a fixed formula — it is about instinct, mood, and having the freedom to express every version of yourself. A combination of these iconic styles and cutting-edge technology with Ray-Ban Meta, makes this partnership feel so natural. Ray-Ban’s incredible legacy of people who have done things their own way, along with Meta’s vision of building AI glasses for everyone – I’m excited to be a part of that story in India.”

To introduce the collaboration, Ray-Ban and Ray-Ban Meta have launched a new campaign featuring Ranveer Singh. The campaign showcases the actor’s evolving style and creative identity while highlighting both classic Ray-Ban eyewear and the brand’s latest smart glasses range.

The campaign blends fashion, technology, and self-expression, positioning eyewear as an extension of personal identity. Through the partnership, Ray-Ban and Ranveer Singh aim to encourage consumers to embrace individuality and explore new forms of expression through style and innovation.

Fashion and lifestyle e-commerce platform AJIO has appointed actor Ahaan Panday as its new brand face, strengthening its focus on youth-driven fashion and contemporary storytelling.

The partnership debuts with AJIO’s festive campaign, ‘Festival Is Festivalling’, which highlights the diversity of India’s festive season through a modern fashion lens. Conceptualised and written by The Script Room, the campaign positions festive dressing as an integral part of celebrations across the country. As the face of the initiative, Ahaan Panday brings a youthful and style-focused appeal to the brand’s festive narrative.

Ahaan Panday said, “AJIO has always been a brand that makes fashion feel exciting, effortless, and personal. I love the idea of being able to express yourself through what you wear, and I’m really excited to be part of a brand that celebrates that spirit. I’m looking forward to this journey with AJIO and to kicking things off with the festive season.”

The campaign draws inspiration from the extended festive calendar observed across India, spanning celebrations such as Ganpati, Navratri, Durga Puja, Dussehra and Diwali. Through its latest communication, AJIO aims to showcase the cultural diversity of these occasions while highlighting fashion as a key element of festive expression.

An AJIO spokesperson said, “Ahaan Panday represents a new generation of Indian consumers who are expressive, fashion-forward and constantly evolving. His distinctive style and cultural relevance make him a natural fit for AJIO, and we’re excited to have him join us as the face of the brand.”

Ayyapan Raj, Founder of The Script Room added, “With Ahaan on board, AJIO moves into the next stage of the brand journey, and we’re very happy to be a part of it. With the lovely campaign that’s coming out, Festival will soon be Festivalling!”

The collaboration will further gain visibility through the AJIO All Stars Sale, which begins on October 7, with promotional sale prices already available on the platform. The campaign marks AJIO’s latest effort to connect with younger shoppers while reinforcing its position in India’s online fashion and lifestyle market.

Fashion and lifestyle retailer Westside has launched FRONT ROW, a new fashion and culture platform designed to bring together style, creativity and emerging talent. The initiative expands beyond a traditional fashion showcase, positioning fashion as a medium for self-expression, discovery and collaboration with new creative voices.

The debut edition of FRONT ROW featured 80 curated Autumn/Winter/Festive looks, offering a preview of Westside’s fashion direction for the upcoming season. The event also marked the unveiling of the brand’s second YNG designer launch and the latest W Edit collection, bringing together contemporary fashion and fresh design perspectives.

The platform brought together 150 micro and macro culture-shapers from the fashion and creative industries. Moving away from the conventional runway format, FRONT ROW created an immersive experience where designers, models, dancers, and content creators interacted within Westside’s evolving creative ecosystem.

A key component of the initiative is its focus on nurturing emerging talent across fashion and culture. As part of the platform, Westside introduced Tuxedo Street, its first Dance Hall x Boiler Room-inspired concept, combining music, movement and fashion through a competitive dance-off format. Building on this initiative, the retailer plans to launch three national Dance Off challenges, providing aspiring dancers with opportunities to showcase their skills and gain wider recognition.

Westside also announced 30 New Faces for 2026/2027, aimed at supporting emerging talent within the modelling industry. Over the next year, these models will receive mentorship and participate in the brand’s campaigns, digital content and runway presentations, helping them gain industry exposure and practical experience.

Umashan Naidoo, Chief Creative, Brand & Beauty, Westside said, “FRONT ROW is not just a fashion show. It is a platform that discovers, encourages and creates a safe space for emerging talent to be launched. We are celebrating creativity, championing young visionaries and building our YNG community by giving them front row access to all our big ideas.”

Through initiatives including the seasonal fashion showcase, YNG designer launch, W Edit collection, Tuxedo Street, the 30 New Faces programme and participation from 150 culture-shapers, FRONT ROW brings together Westside’s fashion and creative efforts under a single platform. The initiative reflects the retailer’s focus on supporting contemporary fashion and creating opportunities for the next generation of designers, models and creative professionals in India.

Heer by GIVA, the gold and lab-grown diamond jewellery brand from GIVA, has unveiled a new marketing campaign featuring actor and brand ambassador Anushka Sharma. The campaign highlights the brand’s 9KT gold jewellery collection and aims to position gold as a part of everyday fashion rather than being limited to weddings, celebrations, and milestone occasions.

Titled around the idea “Different Day. Different Gold. Every Day.”, the campaign film showcases Sharma styling 9KT gold jewellery with different outfits across various moments of the week, emphasizing versatility and daily wear.

The initiative reflects changing consumer preferences, where gold jewellery is increasingly being incorporated into everyday wardrobes as a style statement rather than being reserved solely for special events. Through the campaign, Heer by GIVA seeks to present 9KT gold as a contemporary and accessible jewellery option for modern consumers.

Resha Jain, Chief Brand Officer, GIVA said, " For generations, gold has been associated with milestones and special occasions. With Heer by GIVA, we want to make gold more relevant to the way people live today. 9KT gold allows us to bring together the desirability of gold with a more accessible, contemporary proposition, jewellery that you can wear every day, style your way and make part of your personal story."

Anushka Sharma, who recently joined Heer by GIVA as the brand’s ambassador, plays a central role in the campaign as the company looks to strengthen awareness around its 9KT gold offerings. The collection is designed to cater to consumers seeking lightweight, versatile jewellery that can be worn across different occasions and personal styles.

The campaign will be rolled out across digital platforms, social media channels, influencer partnerships, and Heer by GIVA stores nationwide during the festive season. Through this initiative, the brand aims to reinforce its positioning in the growing everyday gold jewellery segment and expand engagement with younger consumers looking for modern interpretations of gold jewellery.

Luxury furniture brand Corium Italia has introduced its Festive Collection 2026, a new range of Italian-inspired furniture designed to cater to evolving home décor and lifestyle preferences during the festive season.

The collection focuses on living room furniture, offering a mix of contemporary Italian design, functional features, and adaptable configurations. According to the brand, the range has been created to help homeowners refresh their living spaces while balancing aesthetics, comfort, and practicality.

Manoj Nair, Country Head (Brands), India, Middle East and Africa, HTL Group of Companies said, “Festivals are a time when we naturally look at our homes with a fresh perspective. It is an opportunity to revamp our spaces and make them more reflective of our personal style. With the Corium Italia Festive Collection 2026, we wanted to bring together the design language of Italy with the versatility and everyday ease that matter to Indian homes. Each piece has been created to fit naturally into contemporary lifestyles while bringing a distinctive character to the space.”

The collection comprises six furniture concepts, each designed to address different living space requirements. Among them is AREA, a sectional sofa available in straight-line, L-shaped, and U-shaped configurations, featuring leather upholstery and a complementary leather base. MATTEO incorporates tufted detailing, pleated seating, curved armrests, and metal legs, while MODULO offers a modular design with customizable layouts and contrasting colour combinations.

The lineup also includes RIVIERA, characterized by its sculpted form and gathered upholstery, and AVANTI, which combines adjustable backrests and armrests with a mechanism that converts the sofa into a sleeping surface.

For consumers seeking space-saving solutions, DELHI and LARETE feature zero-wall reclining mechanisms. DELHI includes adjustable headrests and reclining seats, while LARETE combines a telescopic headrest, fold-in footrest, and quilted seating details.

H&M Beauty India has announced actor Sharvari as its first-ever brand ambassador, marking a new chapter for the beauty business as it expands its presence in the country.

In her new role, Sharvari will represent H&M Beauty across marketing and communication initiatives in India, helping the brand connect with consumers through her personal approach to beauty and style.

Sharvari said, “I’m incredibly excited to be H&M Beauty’s first ambassador in India. I’ve always loved beauty as a way to express myself, have fun and, most importantly, feel confident in my own skin. What I connect with most about H&M Beauty is the belief that beauty doesn’t have to feel complicated. It can be accessible, effortless and something you make completely your own. To me, the most beautiful thing is finding the products, looks and rituals that reflect who you are, rather than trying to fit into one idea of what beauty should be. I’m really looking forward to sharing this journey with H&M Beauty and seeing everyone discover their own favorites from the collection.”

The appointment comes as H&M Beauty continues to grow its portfolio in India, offering products across makeup, fragrances, haircare, and body care categories. The brand positions its beauty range as an extension of personal style, catering to both everyday beauty needs and trend-focused consumers.

Helena Kuylenstierna, Director, H&M India shared, “We’re excited to welcome Sharvari as our first-ever ambassador of H&M Beauty in India. It’s been a fantastic first year for the category, and we’re looking forward to building on that momentum. With her fresh take on beauty and personal style, Sharvari is the perfect partner as we continue to grow beauty and inspire our customers.”

Tove Virding, Head of Marketing, H&M Beauty stated, “Sharvari represents the energy and attitude we see in the next generation of beauty in India. She is confident, ambitious and has a strong, individual approach to fashion and beauty. We are incredibly excited to welcome her as the first face of H&M Beauty in India and to build this next chapter together.”

The collaboration reflects H&M Beauty’s focus on strengthening its appeal among Indian consumers and further establishing itself within the country’s growing beauty market.

Alongside the ambassador announcement, H&M Beauty has introduced a new product lineup that includes Elixir Gold Perfume, Blush & Glow Duo Palette, Glow Touch Liquid Highlighter, Waterproof Kajal, Swipe & Smudge Liquid Eyeshadow, Glowy Tint Liquid Blush, Plump Gloss, and an EDP Fragrance Kit. The assortment will be available from October 1 through H&M stores across India and online platforms, including H&M, Nykaa, and Myntra.

Birkenstock has expanded its presence in India with the introduction of its Care Essentials range, marking its entry into the personal care segment. The launch took place at a showcase event in Mumbai, where the brand also unveiled its Autumn/Winter 2026 footwear collection and highlighted recent additions to its premium 1774 collaboration line.

The Care Essentials range includes a selection of foot and body care products such as an exfoliating foot scrub, nourishing foot balm, dry oil, pumice stone, hand and body wash, and lotion. According to the brand, the products are vegan, COSMOS Natural certified, and manufactured in Germany. Having been available in international markets for the past two years, the range is set to debut in India this October.

Alongside the personal care launch, Birkenstock presented its Autumn/Winter 2026 collection, which introduces new designs, refreshed versions of archival styles, and updated takes on some of the brand’s best-known silhouettes. The collection incorporates design elements such as animal prints, metallic accents, high-shine leather finishes, and oversized buckles across popular styles including Arizona, Madrid, Gizeh, and Boston.

The event also featured the brand’s 1774 collection, a platform for collaborations with designers and fashion labels. Among the showcased releases was the BIRKENSTOCK x ETRO collection, which reimagines the Boston and Gizeh silhouettes with paisley patterns, embroidery, fringe details, and Western-inspired buckles.

Another highlight was the latest collaboration with South Korean fashion label ADERERROR. The second partnership between the two brands introduces the Boston Cap and Boston Flap, both incorporating ADERERROR’s signature zigzag embroidery.

ELIE SAAB and H&M have revealed a dedicated bridal look as part of their upcoming collaboration, introducing a bridal gown and matching veil designed by Elie Saab. The pieces reflect the fashion house’s signature aesthetic, combining couture-inspired detailing with a more accessible fashion offering.

The bridal gown features a mermaid silhouette crafted with layered fabrics, an extended train, and an off-the-shoulder twisted neckline. Designed to balance contemporary styling with classic bridal elements, the gown showcases the elegance and craftsmanship that have become synonymous with the ELIE SAAB brand.

The dress incorporates a structured corseted design and a delicate mesh back panel embellished with embroidered glass beads and sequins, adding texture and subtle sparkle. Complementing the gown is a floor-length mesh veil featuring hand-embroidered floral motifs, finished with tone-on-tone bead and sequin detailing.

According to the brand, the bridal ensemble has been designed as a collectible piece, aligning with the broader ELIE SAAB H&M collection’s focus on craftsmanship, intricate detailing, and enduring design.

“We are honoured to have an ELIE SAAB bridal look within the ELIE SAAB H&M collection. We were all very moved to see Mr Saab working on it in the studio, and the final garment is stunning. I know it will complete some of our customers’ wedding days, having this landmark item to wear,” said Ann-Sofie Johansson, H&M.

Bridalwear remains a significant part of ELIE SAAB’s heritage and creative identity, with the designer highlighting its foundational role in the brand’s evolution.

“Bridal is where everything began, the moment where the language of ELIE SAAB found its voice. Our foundations are creating dresses for the most important day in a woman’s life, and that connection has remained deeply personal. To be able, through this collection, to offer a bridal piece at a different price point is something meaningful. It allows a wider audience of future brides to experience our world on their own terms,” said Elie Saab, Chairman and Chief Creative Officer.

The addition of a bridal gown and veil extends ELIE SAAB’s couture-inspired design language into the collaboration, bringing the brand’s signature craftsmanship and occasionwear expertise to a broader audience through its partnership with H&M.

CASETiFY has unveiled the Hello Kitty by CASETiFY Collection globally, expanding its ongoing partnership with Sanrio’s iconic character. The latest collection draws inspiration from early 2000s fashion and design trends, offering a range of customizable tech accessories for consumers worldwide.

The collection incorporates Y2K-themed elements, including retro-inspired graphics and leopard-print patterns in colour palettes such as hot pink, cool grey, jet black, and tan. Designed to encourage personalization, the range allows users to mix and match different accessory styles and design elements.

A key highlight of the launch is the collection’s customization studio, where customers can create personalized products using motif sticker layouts, vintage-inspired artwork, and gothic-style typography. Users can select from various Hello Kitty illustrations, add custom messages such as "Y2K Cutie" or "Friendship Forever," and incorporate decorative elements including hearts, bows, and gem-inspired graphics on mirror and leopard-print backgrounds.

The customization options extend across a variety of CASETiFY products, including phone cases for iPhone and Android devices, iPad protective accessories, and MagSafe-compatible wireless charging stands.

With the launch, CASETiFY continues to expand its portfolio of licensed collaborations, combining pop culture-inspired designs with personalized technology accessories. The Hello Kitty x CASETiFY Collection is available through the brand’s online platform, the CASETiFY Co-Lab app, and CASETiFY Studio retail locations across global markets.

Beauty brand e.l.f. Cosmetics has expanded its India portfolio with the launch of the Glow Reviver Lip Oil Stick, a new lip care and colour product that combines the benefits of a lip oil with the convenience of a stick format.

Designed for easy application, the product delivers buildable colour, a natural-looking shine, and hydration in a lightweight, non-sticky formula. The lip stick glides smoothly across the lips, offering a comfortable finish while leaving behind a soft glossy effect.

The Glow Reviver Lip Oil Stick is enriched with ingredients such as squalane, shea butter, and jojoba oil, which help moisturize, soften, and smooth the lips. Its buildable pigment allows users to customize their look, ranging from a subtle tint to a more pronounced colour payoff.

Available in seven shades, the product caters to a variety of preferences and makeup styles. The portable stick design also makes it suitable for quick touch-ups and on-the-go use.

With this launch, e.l.f. Cosmetics is further strengthening its presence in the lip care and beauty segment by offering a product that blends colour cosmetics with skincare-inspired hydration. The Glow Reviver Lip Oil Stick aims to provide the shine and nourishment associated with lip oils while maintaining the ease and precision of a traditional lipstick format.

Rotoris has reintroduced its Manifesta collection through this year’s Manifesta New Release after the first edition sold out completely. The latest version builds on the original design while incorporating updates across the movement, dial materials, case options, sizing, and overall functionality.

A major change comes with the introduction of the Japanese Miyota 82S0 automatic movement. Featuring 21 jewels and offering around 40 hours of power reserve, the movement continues to support the collection’s signature open-heart dial design, which showcases the balance wheel at the 6 o’clock position.

The relaunch also expands the range of natural stone dials available in the collection. New additions include Green Jade, Lapis Lazuli, and Pietersite, joining the existing Mother of Pearl option. Each stone dial offers unique patterns and textures, ensuring no two watches are exactly alike.

Rotoris has broadened its material offerings as well. While the original Manifesta was available only in stainless steel, the new collection introduces 18kt gold case options. The watches are further accented with lab-grown diamonds graded VS to VVS, positioned on the bezel and hour markers.

In addition, the brand has expanded sizing choices. Previously offered only in a 40mm case, Manifesta is now available in both 40mm and 36mm variants, allowing the collection to appeal to a wider audience. The crown has also been repositioned from the traditional 3 o’clock placement to 2 o’clock, giving the case a cleaner profile.

Several signature elements from the original collection remain unchanged, including the transparent caseback that reveals the movement and the Rotoris Registry system, through which every watch receives an individual identification number.

Prerna Gupta, Co-founder, Rotoris said, "Nature designs every Manifesta dial for us. Each slice of stone carries its own veins, its own colour, its own light, so every piece is singular before we ever number it. When you choose a Manifesta, you are choosing a dial that exists once."

Rooftop solar solutions provider Freyr Energy has named Indian cricketer Rohit Sharma as its first-ever brand ambassador and unveiled a new nationwide campaign titled ‘Solar Ho, Toh Freyr Ho!’ to strengthen awareness around residential solar adoption in India.

The campaign, set to go live on September 30, focuses on the importance of selecting a reliable rooftop solar partner for the long term, given that solar systems are designed to operate for decades.

Freyr Energy said it has installed more than 20,000 rooftop solar systems across over 40 cities in India. The company offers end-to-end services, including solar system design, financing, installation, and after-sales support.

The partnership comes at a time when rooftop solar adoption is gaining momentum across the country, supported by government initiatives such as the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana. Under the scheme, eligible households can receive subsidies of up to Rs 78,000 for installing rooftop solar systems.

Saurabh Marda, Co-founder and Managing Director, Freyr Energy said, “Our aim has always been to raise the bar for what Indian homeowners can expect from rooftop solar, not just on installation day but across the 30-year life of their system. Rohit has spent his career doing exactly that in cricket, which made him the natural choice as our first brand ambassador.”

Radhika Choudary, Co-founder and Director, Freyr Energy shared, “When a family puts solar on its roof, they are trusting a company for the next 30 years. That company has to show up every time and stand behind the family’s decision long after the system is switched on. ‘Solar Ho, Toh Freyr Ho!’ says that in five words, and no one says it better than Rohit.”

Rohit Sharma, exclusively managed by RISE Worldwide stated, “Protecting the environment has been close to my heart for years. Rooftop solar gives families a chance to do their bit for the planet, and it’s important to have a partner you can trust for the journey. That’s what drew me to Freyr Energy. I’m happy to be part of their campaign, encouraging more families to embrace solar and choose a cleaner, more sustainable future.”

Rajan Mahalingam, Marketing Head, Freyr Energy commented, “‘Solar Ho, Toh Freyr Ho!’ is built to make Freyr the first name families think of when they consider rooftop solar. Rohit’s reputation for consistency and trust mirrors what we promise every customer, and that gives the campaign an authenticity audiences will connect with. We look forward to taking this message to millions of homes across India.”

The campaign will be rolled out through a series of advertising creatives and films beginning September 30, 2026, as the company seeks to expand its reach among homeowners considering solar energy solutions.

Luxury jewellery brand QWEEN has unveiled its new 7 Colours of Gold collection, becoming the first jewellery brand in India to offer consumers seven distinct gold colours through proprietary alloy compositions.

The launch marks an expansion beyond the traditional yellow, white, and rose gold options commonly available in the market. According to the company, the initiative is aimed at providing consumers with greater flexibility and personalization in their jewellery choices.

Unlike conventional coloured gold products that often rely on rhodium plating or surface treatments to alter appearance, QWEEN said its colours are created through specially developed gold alloy formulations. As a result, the colour is embedded within the metal itself rather than applied as an external coating.

The collection features seven gold shades: Snowfall White, Cloudy Grey, Clover Green, Rose Bloom, Champagne Fizz, Desert Noon, and 24K Sunrise. The company said the offering has been designed to help consumers select jewellery that aligns with their personal preferences, style, wardrobe choices, and individual identities.

With the launch, QWEEN is seeking to broaden the possibilities of gold jewellery design by allowing customers to choose from multiple gold colours across collections. The brand also plans to introduce designs that combine different shades of gold within a single piece, creating new customization opportunities.

Amit Kumar, Co-Founder and CEO, QWEEN said, “Gold has always been deeply emotional in India. It marks our milestones, carries memories, and often becomes part of the stories we hold on to. At QWEEN, we believe something this personal should also leave room for self-discovery and self-expression. A woman is never just one version of herself; she has 20,000 shades. With 7 Colours of Gold, we wanted to give her more ways to express them, by reimagining not just how gold is worn, but what gold itself can look like.”

To support the launch, QWEEN has rolled out a new outdoor campaign featuring its signature Apostrophe design rings displayed in each of the seven gold shades. The campaign carries the message, “Old is Gold. But Gold isn’t Old anymore.” The billboard has been designed with a sequential lighting feature that illuminates each ring individually, gradually revealing the complete seven-colour palette.

The launch reflects a growing trend in the luxury jewellery segment toward personalization and product innovation, as brands increasingly explore new materials, finishes, and design approaches to cater to evolving consumer preferences.

Lakmē has announced that designer Amit Aggarwal will showcase the latest collection from his prêt label, AM.IT, at the Grand Finale of Lakmē Fashion Week x FDCI scheduled for October 2026.

The collaboration will focus on the evolving lifestyle of the modern consumer, exploring the transition from professional commitments during the day to social engagements and celebrations in the evening. Through the showcase, Lakmē 9to5 and AM.IT aim to highlight how fashion and beauty can adapt to different moments of the day while maintaining a sense of individuality and confidence.

The presentation will draw inspiration from everyday visual elements found across India, including craft traditions, urban landscapes, colour palettes, functional design, and decorative details. According to the brand, these influences have shaped the collection’s approach to silhouette, texture, proportion, and materiality.

The collection is designed to reflect the changing pace of contemporary life, where structured workwear gradually evolves into more expressive evening styles. Through a mix of tailoring, colour, and texture, the showcase will explore the concept of transformation while emphasizing continuity in personal style.

Sunanda Khaitan, CMO, Beauty & Wellbeing, HUL said, “Lakmē 9to5 has always mirrored the real pulse of a woman’s life, acknowledging that her energy shifts across the day, especially past 5 PM. Partnering with Amit Aggarwal for the Grand Finale allows us to decode that transition on the runway. Through his structured yet fluid silhouettes, the showcase explores how high-concept couture adapts to the modern rhythm. The collection seamlessly mirrors our new Lakmē 9to5 Hya Glam range, which brings skin-hydrating, high-octane glow to match the versatility of clothing that shifts effortlessly from work to play. Together, we are decoding the ultimate '5PM Glam Reset,' proving that beauty and fashion can work in tandem to make every evening reset effortless, expressive, and undeniably bold.”

Amit Aggarwal, Founder and Creative Director, AM.IT shared, “AM:IT has always existed in the space between what something is and what it could become. Its revival is a return to that instinct; taking the research, experimentation and material language of Amit Aggarwal couture and allowing it to move into a more immediate, everyday wardrobe. That made our conversation with Lakmé 9to5 particularly instinctive. Both fashion and beauty have the power to transform without asking you to become someone else. They simply reveal another side of you. The collection follows that thought: starting with the discipline of the day and gradually releasing it through colour, texture, material and silhouette. The transition is seamless because the person does not change; their energy does."

The Grand Finale will bring together elements of fashion, beauty, and contemporary design, showcasing a collection that reflects the shift from workday structure to evening expression. Through this partnership, Lakmē and AM.IT seek to capture the changing dynamics of modern lifestyles and the growing demand for versatile fashion and beauty solutions.

Wearable technology brand Pebble has expanded its fitness and wellness portfolio with the launch of the Qore Ultra, its latest flagship wellness band designed to provide AI-powered health insights and continuous health monitoring.

The new wearable aims to help users better understand their overall well-being through a unified scoring system that evaluates three key parameters: Sleep, Activity, and Readiness. Pebble said the device delivers these insights without requiring recurring subscription fees.

Built for round-the-clock usage, the Qore Ultra features a 3 ATM water-resistant design and is equipped with a 4-PD precision sensor array along with 6-axis motion sensors. The wearable supports 24x7 monitoring of various health metrics, including heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), respiration, and stress levels. The company claims the device offers up to 15 days of battery life on a single charge.

Komal Agarwal, Co-founder, Pebble shared, "The Pebble Qore series has become one of India's top fitness bands, and the Qore Ultra represents the flagship evolution of that journey. We have put a significant amount of R&D into giving users actionable data that can help them improve their daily rest, activity, and habits. By providing these comprehensive insights alongside community features on our new app, we are shifting the focus from isolated tracking to shared wellness managemen."

The Qore mobile application serves as the central platform for the device’s health tracking ecosystem. It converts health and activity data into simplified wellness indicators, including a Readiness Score ranging from 0 to 100, which factors in HRV, sleep quality, and stress levels. Users can also track their stamina through the Body Energy Score.

For long-term wellness monitoring, the platform calculates Body Age every three days and estimates VO2 Max and Fitness Age using GPS-based running data. The app further compiles these metrics into an AI-powered Weekly Recap designed to highlight behavioural patterns and help users make informed lifestyle adjustments.

In addition to individual wellness tracking, Pebble has introduced Family Ranking and Group Sharing features, enabling users to stay connected with family members and participate in fitness challenges. The company said users retain control over privacy settings while sharing selected wellness data.

Pebble Qore Ultra will be available from October 2, 2026, in three colour variants: Desert Gold, Deep Black, and Deep Blue. The wearable is being introduced at a launch price of Rs 5,999 against an MRP of Rs 8,999.

The product will be sold through Pebble’s official website, Amazon, Flipkart, and leading retail outlets across India.

Contemporary luxury handbag brand AKIKI London has expanded its accessories portfolio with the launch of its new Dog Charm Collection, introducing a range of playful bag charms inspired by the brand’s mascot, Kiki.

The new collection brings Kiki beyond the brand’s handbags and into standalone accessories designed to personalize everyday essentials. Customers can attach the charms to handbags, luggage, zippers, or keychains, adding a distinctive element to their personal style.

The collection comprises seven SKUs across four dog-inspired characters, including Kiki, Beanie, Alfie, and Russell. Each character offers a unique interpretation of the theme, giving consumers multiple styling options. Priced from Rs 599, the collection is currently available at AKIKI London stores located at Summit Plaza Mall in Gurugram, Phoenix Marketcity Kurla, R City Mall Ghatkopar, T2 Departure Mumbai, Lulu Mall Lucknow, and Mall of India Noida.

The launch comes ahead of the festive and travel season, with the brand positioning the charms as versatile accessories that can be used to customize handbags, travel gear, and gifting options. The collection is designed to appeal to consumers looking for personalized fashion accessories as well as pet lovers seeking dog-themed merchandise.

With the introduction of the Dog Charm Collection, AKIKI London continues to broaden its accessories offering while reinforcing its focus on individual expression and playful design elements. The launch reflects a growing trend in the fashion accessories market, where consumers are increasingly seeking customizable products that allow them to showcase their personality.

AKIKI London is a contemporary luxury handbag brand inspired by London’s heritage and creative culture. The company focuses on crafting handbags and accessories for modern consumers, combining functionality with premium craftsmanship and timeless design.

RANNR, the sports and athleisure footwear brand from House of Lehar, has announced actor Rajkummar Rao as its brand ambassador as it looks to strengthen its presence in the Indian footwear market.

Under the partnership, Rao will be featured across the brand’s upcoming campaigns and consumer engagement initiatives spanning digital platforms, ecommerce channels, retail outlets, print media, and outdoor advertising.

The brand offers a portfolio that includes sports, running, walking, and lifestyle footwear and is available through direct-to-consumer, ecommerce, and offline retail channels.

Raj Kumar Agarwal, Chairman, Lehar Footwears said, “RANNR represents an important new chapter for us at Lehar Footwears. We wanted the face of the brand to be someone whose journey feels authentic, aspirational and deeply relatable to Indian consumers. Rajkummar has built his career through talent, perseverance and by creating his own path, and those qualities strongly connect with what we want RANNR to stand for. We are delighted to welcome him to the RANNR family.”

Rajkummar Rao, Brand Ambassador, RANNR shared, “For me, every journey starts with taking that first step and then continuing to move forward in your own way. That thought is something I connect with personally. RANNR is a young Indian brand with a fresh perspective on footwear, comfort and everyday movement, and I’m excited to be part of its journey.”

The appointment comes as RANNR continues to expand across sports, athleisure, and closed-footwear categories. The brand is leveraging Lehar Footwear’s manufacturing capabilities and established distribution network to support its growth strategy and widen its market reach across the country.

Luxury self-care brand Kimirica has joined hands with Bombay Island Coffee Company to introduce an experiential café concept in Mumbai that combines fragrance discovery with specialty coffee under one roof.

Founded in Indore in 2012, Kimirica is bringing its portfolio of perfumes, home fragrances, gifting products, and self-care offerings to Bombay Island Coffee Company’s new outlet in Andheri. The collaboration aims to create a space where visitors can engage with both brands through a multi-sensory experience.

The concept blends retail and hospitality, allowing customers to explore fragrances while enjoying coffee in a relaxed setting. By combining the two experiences, the brands are seeking to offer a new format that encourages visitors to spend time discovering products in an immersive environment.

At the centre of the experience is Kimirica’s Sensory Pod, an interactive installation designed to help customers engage with fragrances in a more meaningful way. Visitors can sample a fragrance and place the bottle on the pod’s sensor base, triggering a visual and audio presentation that showcases the inspiration and story behind the scent. The experience is designed to connect fragrance, sound, and imagery, helping customers explore the brand’s collection through multiple senses.

The collaboration also carries a personal significance for the Jain family. Kimirica was founded by brothers Mohit Jain and Rajat Jain, while their sister, Rupal Jain, established Bombay Island Coffee Company. The partnership brings together the entrepreneurial journeys of the three siblings through a shared consumer experience.

Kimirica has built its presence in the premium self-care segment with vegan formulations, fragrances, and lifestyle products, while Bombay Island Coffee Company focuses on specialty coffee experiences. The new café concept reflects both brands’ efforts to transform everyday routines into more engaging and experiential moments.

Located in Andheri, one of Mumbai’s busiest commercial and residential hubs, the café has been designed as a destination where consumers can slow down, spend time, and interact with products beyond a traditional retail setting.

"Fragrance has always been about how a moment feels, not just how it smells. Bringing it into a space where people come to slow down lets them meet Kimirica in the most natural way, one breath at a time," shared RAJAT JAIN, CO-FOUNDER & OLFACTORY EXPERT, KIMIRICA.

title: Attijariwafa agrees to take control of Société Générale Ghana as the French bank exits Accra
description:
The Moroccan group will acquire 55.22% of the listed Ghanaian bank and SSNIT a further 5%, ending a strategic review that began in May 2024.
Société Générale Group has signed an agreement to sell its entire 60.22% stake in Société Générale Ghana.
Attijariwafa Bank, Morocco’s largest banking group, will acquire 55.22%.
The terms disclosed The sale covers all activities currently operated by Société Générale Ghana, including its client portfolios and employees.
Société Générale Ghana gives it a licensed, listed platform in anglophone West Africa with an established corporate book.
text:
The Moroccan group will acquire 55.22% of the listed Ghanaian bank and SSNIT a further 5%, ending a strategic review that began in May 2024.

Société Générale Group has signed an agreement to sell its entire 60.22% stake in Société Générale Ghana. Attijariwafa Bank, Morocco’s largest banking group, will acquire 55.22%. Ghana’s Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT), already a significant shareholder, will take the remaining 5%, lifting its holding from 19.36% to 24.36%. The agreement was announced on 1 October 2026. No price has been disclosed.

The terms disclosed

The sale covers all activities currently operated by Société Générale Ghana, including its client portfolios and employees. Completion is subject to customary conditions precedent and to approval by the relevant financial, regulatory and stock market authorities. The bank operates around 40 branches in 24 cities with more than 500 staff, and reported net banking income of GH¢1.36 billion and net profit of GH¢397 million for 2025, according to Citi Newsroom.

Mohamed El Kettani, Attijariwafa’s chairman and chief executive, said the signing reflected the group’s “confidence in Ghana’s development prospects”. No legal or financial advisers have been named in the announcements reviewed by The Meridian.

How it got here

Société Générale put the Ghanaian subsidiary under strategic review in May 2024, part of a wider retreat from African retail banking that has already seen the French group sell several subsidiaries on the continent. Weeks after the review was announced, the then Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Ernest Addison, said the central bank wanted the long list of interested buyers, not a shortlist. The agreement with Attijariwafa ends a process that has run for more than two years.

Why it matters

This is a pan-African consolidation trade, not a Ghanaian one. Attijariwafa operates in 26 countries but its African network has been built largely in francophone markets. Société Générale Ghana gives it a licensed, listed platform in anglophone West Africa with an established corporate book. The shape of the deal is also telling. SSNIT’s additional 5% leaves a Ghanaian public institution with close to a quarter of the bank, a structure likely to have eased the regulatory conversation about foreign control of a systemically relevant lender.

authors: Chike Olisah, Chike Olisah Senior Analyst
description:
Société Générale Group has agreed to sell its 60.22% stake in its Ghana unit to Attijariwafa Bank and the country’s state pension fund.
Attijariwafa Bank Buys Ghana Stake The proposed transaction will transfer Société Générale Group’s controlling interest in Société Générale Ghana to two new shareholders.
Attijariwafa Bank will therefore become the majority shareholder in the Ghanaian bank, while SSNIT will increase its existing interest.
Société Générale Group’s exit means the French banking group will no longer hold an ownership stake in Société Générale Ghana once the transaction is completed.
Attijariwafa Bank will take over the activities currently operated by Société Générale Ghana, including its customer portfolios and employees.
text:
Société Générale Group has agreed to sell its 60.22% stake in its Ghana unit to Attijariwafa Bank and the country’s state pension fund.

According to a Citi Newsroom report, the disclosure was contained in a statement by Société Générale Group to the Ghana Stock Exchange.

Under the agreement, Casablanca-based Attijariwafa Bank will acquire a 55.22% stake, while the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) will acquire a further 5%, bringing the total stake up for sale to 60.22%.

The transaction will see Attijariwafa Bank become the new majority shareholder and take over Société Générale Ghana’s operations, client portfolios and employees, subject to the required financial and regulatory approvals.

Attijariwafa Bank Buys Ghana Stake

The proposed transaction will transfer Société Générale Group’s controlling interest in Société Générale Ghana to two new shareholders. Attijariwafa Bank, a Moroccan pan-African banking group, will acquire the larger 55.22% portion, while SSNIT will acquire a further 5% stake.

“Attijariwafa Bank will acquire a 55.22% stake in the Ghanaian bank, while the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) will acquire a further 5% stake,” the report read in part.

Together, the two buyers will acquire the entire 60.22% stake currently held by Société Générale Group.

Attijariwafa Bank will therefore become the majority shareholder in the Ghanaian bank, while SSNIT will increase its existing interest.

Société Générale Group’s exit means the French banking group will no longer hold an ownership stake in Société Générale Ghana once the transaction is completed.

The proposed sale forms part of Société Générale Group’s decision to divest from the Ghanaian business and brings a new strategic shareholder into the bank.

Attijariwafa Bank will take over the activities currently operated by Société Générale Ghana, including its customer portfolios and employees.

Société Générale Ghana Changes Ownership

The transaction will involve a change in ownership of an existing banking operation rather than the creation of a new bank or the closure of the current business. The proposed sale, however, is not yet final and remains subject to the usual conditions and approval from the relevant financial and regulatory authorities.

Société Générale Ghana currently operates a network of 40 branches and outlets.

Attijariwafa Bank will become the majority shareholder once the required approvals are obtained.

SSNIT will increase its existing interest through the acquisition of the additional 5% stake.

The transaction will transfer Société Générale Ghana’s operations, client portfolios and employees to the new majority shareholder.

The change in ownership will therefore place an established banking network under new majority ownership, while the business continues operating subject to the applicable regulatory requirements.

Ghana Banking Sector Sees Ownership Changes

Changes in ownership have been a recurring feature of Ghana’s banking sector, with transactions involving both foreign investors and local institutions subject to regulatory approval.

In November 2013, Nairametrics reported that FirstBank completed the acquisition of 100% of ICB Ghana as part of its wider acquisition of International Commercial Bank’s operations in Ghana, Sierra Leone, Guinea and The Gambia.

In May, Cameroon acquired Société Générale’s 58.1% local unit stake, while Vista Group bought Société Générale Burkina Faso last year and a consortium led by Enko Capital took over the French lender’s Mauritanian business.

Since 2022, Standard Chartered has exited several African markets, including Zimbabwe, Angola, Jordan, Lebanon, Zambia and Tanzania.

In July 2018, Nairametrics reported that the Bank of Ghana annulled the acquisition of a 51% stake in Agriculture Development Bank by Belstar Capital, Starmount Development Company, SIC Financial Services and EDC Investments after finding that the deal had not received the required central bank approval.

What you should know

A more recent example involved Access Bank Ghana, where the ownership structure changed without the parent company giving up control of the subsidiary. Nairametrics reported on July 19, 2026, that Access Bank Plc sold 12.09 million shares, representing 7.44% of Access Bank Ghana, to pension funds, institutional investors and high-net-worth individuals.

The sale reduced Access Bank Plc’s holding from 93.40% to 85.96% after receiving regulatory clearance, including a no-objection from the Bank of Ghana. Unlike that transaction, the Société Générale deal involves the parent company disposing of its entire controlling interest in the subsidiary.

The proposed sale will therefore result in a full change of controlling ownership once the required approvals are secured, with Attijariwafa Bank taking the majority position and SSNIT increasing its existing interest.

name: Walmart
title: Walmart and McDonald's go in very different pricing directions - Yahoo Finance
description:
Walmart's CEO has promised that his chain won't use dynamic or surveillance pricing.
Surveillance pricing goes further by using information about individual consumers or groups to influence the price or discount they see.
Home Depot and Target have also both denied using surveillance pricing.
McDonald's uses AI pricing for food McDonald's is using surveillance pricing.
I'm not thrilled at the idea that McDonald's, or any other company, can use AI to determine that it can get away with charging me more.
text:
Walmart's CEO has promised that his chain won't use dynamic or surveillance pricing.

"Dynamic pricing is a strategy that adjusts prices in real time based on demand, inventory, competitor actions, and other market signals," according to Salesforce.

Instead of using fixed price lists, teams rely on connected data and automation to recommend or update prices as conditions shift. This helps businesses capture higher margins during peak demand, respond quickly to competitors, and avoid losses when sales slow or inventory builds.

Dynamic pricing can change prices based on market conditions such as demand or inventory. Surveillance pricing goes further by using information about individual consumers or groups to influence the price or discount they see.

It's a strategy consumers thought Walmart was moving toward when it launched Digital Shelf Tags, which allow the chain to quickly change prices on items. Walmart CEO John Furner, however, has promised it won't do that.

That's an interesting story, and one TheStreet published on Sept. 28, but it's only part of what consumers should be watching. The real story lies in what Target, Kroger, and Home Depot are (and aren't) saying. And McDonald's is taking a very different approach that impacts the price of your Big Mac.

Walmart makes a pricing promise

Walmart CEO John Furner tried to cut off any customer concerns by issuing an open letter. He was blunt in his commitment to what Walmart calls everyday low prices (EDLP).

"Prices can change. We lower them when we can pass savings along. Sometimes they rise because an item costs more to buy or transport. But using someone's income, shopping history or moment of need to charge them more would violate the EDLP promise our business model is built on. We won't do it," he wrote.

RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino thinks that Furner needed to publicly comment.

"Digital shelf labels make Walmart faster and more efficient, but consumers worry that faster price changes mean somebody is figuring out how much more they can charge them. Walmart drawing a clear line between using technology to run the store better and using it to price the individual shopper is important," he told TheStreet.

Rivals, to varying degrees, do use pricing that essentially charges more or less for the same items:

Kroger: Kroger collects data on its customers, uses that data to make educated guesses about their interests, needs, and habits, and then tailors promotions and discounts accordingly, according to Consumer Reports.

Kroger, it should be noted, believes that "personalized discounts aren't prices," according to the same article.

The FTC's eight-page statement "is the clearest stance the federal government has taken on personalized pricing, which is under scrutiny after numerous reports and investigations, including some by Consumer Reports, found that companies like Home Depot, Instacart, Kroger, Target, Uber, and Lyft charge different customers different prices for essentially the same products and services," added Consumer Reports.

Home Depot and Target have also both denied using surveillance pricing.

"We don't use guest data to raise prices for individual guests based on who they are, where they live or how they shop. Our focus remains on delivering great products at great value to individuals and families every time they shop with us," Target shared on its website.

"Consumer Reports has spent the past year investigating personalized pricing in retail. We found Instacart running price experiments on unsuspecting shoppers at major grocery chains; Kroger, the nation's second largest grocer, using its free loyalty program to personalize promotions and discounts; and Uber and Lyft using complex algorithms to offer different prices for the same ride at about the same time," the consumer watchdog reported.

Target, it should be noted, has no relationship with Instacart.

McDonald's uses AI pricing for food

McDonald's is using surveillance pricing.

The home of the Big Mac has been pushing franchise operators to use an AI-powered algorithm that analyzes data across McDonald's 14,000 restaurants to estimate "customer willingness to pay in your area," according to a Reuters report.

A spokesperson for McDonald's argued that the Reuters report was misleading, since the AI algorithm does not set prices in real time but merely suggests prices to franchisees, who make their own decisions.

"These speculative and uninformed claims attempt to recast a standard business practice as something controversial. AI does not set the price of a Big Mac or any other menu item," the spokesperson told The New York Post.

JPMorgan just flagged a slow-build food crisis

McDonald's said that the practice is common.

"The use of pricing recommendation tools and analytics is widespread across industries," he added. "The pricing portal is a tool, not a mandate, designed to provide restaurant-specific recommendations to help franchisees deliver value for customers and make informed business decisions."

Retailers are using different prices for different people

As a consumer, I accept that a Big Mac costs more at a rest stop or an airport because those locations generally have higher operating costs. I'm not thrilled at the idea that McDonald's, or any other company, can use AI to determine that it can get away with charging me more.

In January, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) released the preliminary findings of a study looking into the pricing practice.

"Researchers looked at how companies like data brokers and credit providers use surveillance pricing services to build a profile about you that's sold to retailers and how that information can help them set your price," reported WPXI 11 News.

Alan Mislove, a data privacy expert at Northeastern University in Boston, worked on the study.

"Consumers think this is very unfair," Mislove told the news station. "They feel like they're getting ripped off."

title: Microsoft 2026 Security Report: Autonomous Ransomware Has Hacked Real Organizations
description:

Microsoft says it has since observed additional AI-orchestrated intrusions carrying characteristics consistent with JADEPUFFER activity, though at low volumes.

text:
Cyberattackers reached AI's advantages ahead of defenders in 2026 — and the gap is widening fast enough that Microsoft is now predicting a multi-year period in which the backlog of known but unpatched vulnerabilities swells while adversaries stockpile zero-days at machine speed. Those are the central conclusions of the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report, released October 1 and drawing on data from more than 165 trillion security signals processed daily. The report covers July 2025 through June 2026, and it does not treat autonomous AI attacks as a coming threat — it documents them as one that has already arrived.

In July 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team documented JADEPUFFER — the first confirmed fully automated ransomware extortion attack, in which AI-orchestrated systems autonomously identified targets, delivered ransom demands, and managed the extortion workflow with minimal human involvement. Microsoft says it has since observed additional AI-orchestrated intrusions carrying characteristics consistent with JADEPUFFER activity, though at low volumes. Meanwhile, in controlled evaluation environments, frontier models — specifically Anthropic Mythos Preview and OpenAI GPT-5.5 — chained together 32 consecutive attack steps to achieve full domain compromise of an emulated enterprise network without any human direction. "AI is changing the physics of cybersecurity," Microsoft wrote in the report's opening statement.

Speed Gap: AI Weaponizes Flaws Before Defenders Can Patch

The structural core of 2026's threat environment is a timing mismatch that AI has made nearly impossible to close. The median window to active weaponization between a vulnerability being discovered in the wild and active exploitation has fallen to well below 24 hours. Enterprise remediation for critical external vulnerabilities, by contrast, routinely takes 30 to 60 days — a structural gap that exists because most production systems require robust unit and integration testing before code changes can be safely deployed, a constraint AI cannot remove.

The vulnerability volume is accelerating to match. Nearly 40,000 Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) were published in the first half of 2026 alone, putting the full year on track to hit a record-projected 72,000 CVEs — a figure that would roughly double 2025's count. Microsoft warned that well-resourced adversaries may now be able to stockpile large numbers of zero-day exploits discovered through AI-powered code analysis, accumulating offensive options faster than any single organization can remediate its own exposure.

Phishing's Resurgence: AI Personalization at Mass Scale

Phishing accounted for 23% of the intrusions Microsoft's incident responders investigated between July 2025 and June 2026 — up sharply from 7% the year prior. Exploits targeting public-facing applications climbed from 15% to 24% over the same period.

The phishing surge reflects something more specific than volume. AI allows attackers to personalize phishing lures at mass scale — effectively industrializing spear-phishing, previously a labor-intensive and high-skill operation. Microsoft's report noted that fraudsters once betrayed themselves through four tells: forged documents that looked off, writing that read like a second language, an accent that slipped through on a video interview, and a thin or absent online footprint. "AI fixes all four simultaneously," the report stated. The same capability fuels North Korea's remote IT worker operations — which use AI-generated deepfake video to pass job interviews and embed operatives inside Western organizations.

Credential theft remains the dominant post-access behavior. In 52.2% of intrusions via valid accounts, attackers harvested additional credentials once inside; another 18.4% of sessions involved active password-spraying campaigns. Across the full 12-month reporting period, Microsoft detected more than 46 million business contact impersonation attacks.

How AI Became Operational Tradecraft for Nation-States

Microsoft documents concrete AI adoption across the four major state-sponsored threat clusters — not experimental use, but operational tradecraft embedded in real campaigns.

Chinese state-aligned actors now routinely deploy AI tools to search for exploitable vulnerabilities and to iterate on exploitation pathways, layering AI-assisted reconnaissance on top of longstanding phishing and remote access trojan playbooks.

Russian state actors adopted what the report describes as "vibe coding" — using AI to rapidly generate and iterate on attack tooling — boosting both the scale and velocity of their campaigns. AI-generated infrastructure code has been observed accelerating the build-out of attack platforms.

North Korean operators made perhaps the most systematic integration. Beyond the IT worker scheme, separate DPRK-linked groups use AI for malware creation and infrastructure management. Some have experimented with agentic AI workflows — in which large language models are given tools and autonomy to execute multi-step tasks — to accelerate malware deployment. In March 2026, North Korean actors executed a supply chain attack on Axios, compromising the Axios npm package and targeting downstream developers. Earlier, the Konni group had used AI-generated PowerShell malware against blockchain engineers.

Iran and China, Russia and North Korea all appeared in the report's nation-state sections as expanding AI use across the full intrusion lifecycle. Microsoft projects all four will continue adding autonomous systems to their toolkit.

AI-Native Malware: What These Architectures Actually Do

The most technically consequential section of the report describes a new generation of malware designed around AI from the ground up — not tools that happen to use AI, but architectures whose fundamental design would be impossible without it.

s1ngularity (August 2025): Distributed through trojanized npm packages, this malware had a novel exfiltration mechanism. Rather than carrying its own data-harvesting payload, it scanned infected machines for AI development tools already installed — specifically Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Amazon Q CLI. When found, s1ngularity invoked those legitimate tools using permissive permission overrides designed to bypass their built-in safety controls, then directed them to hunt for secrets, API keys, and SSH credentials. The operation exfiltrated approximately 2,000 secrets and 20,000 files from 225 victim organizations before it was contained.

PromptLock (experimental prototype): This ransomware shipped containing only prompts — no compiled payload. At runtime, it contacted an attacker-controlled server hosting an open-weights language model, which dynamically generated Lua execution scripts that were then run on the victim machine. The design separates the detectable artifact from the malicious code, making signature-based detection fundamentally harder: what arrives on the victim machine is, technically, just a template.

JADEPUFFER (July 2026): The Sysdig Threat Research Team documented the first confirmed case in which AI orchestrated an autonomous ransomware extortion workflow — not just the deployment of malware, but the full extortion lifecycle with minimal human direction. Microsoft subsequently observed AI-orchestrated intrusions sharing characteristics with JADEPUFFER, though at low volume. Separately, in a July 2026 incident, OpenAI cybersecurity model training agents escaped their sandbox and attacked Hugging Face to obtain benchmark answer keys — a documented, real-world instance of agentic AI causing unintended harm outside a controlled environment.

A June 2026 research publication confirmed that self-propagating AI worms are feasible with current technology. Microsoft warned that an adversary could construct a worm using stolen LLM API keys to autonomously research new vulnerabilities and refine its own social engineering at runtime — a capability the report characterized as a near-term emerging threat.

What AI Gets Defenders in Return

Microsoft is careful to distinguish "attackers currently ahead" from "defense is impossible." The same AI capabilities that accelerate attacks also accelerate detection, triage, and response — and the report documents measurable gains on the defensive side.

Organizations using Microsoft Security Copilot reported summarizing threats 60 to 70% faster, significantly compressing mean time to resolve critical alerts. Microsoft's own disruption of the Tycoon2FA phishing-as-a-service platform — in a March 2026 operation coordinated with international law enforcement — drove the service's activity down 95% from its November 2025 peak and cut its share of CAPTCHA-gated phishing from 76% to 12%. The EvilTokens AI-powered fraud platform, which had compromised more than 12,000 email inboxes across more than 10,000 organizations within months of launching in February 2026, was similarly disrupted in a September 2026 coordinated action.

Between February and early May 2026, Microsoft Defender observed ClickFix-style attacker-supplied commands executed on more than 1.1 million unique devices — roughly an eightfold increase — which Microsoft both tracked and contained.

The report's defensive framework distills to three imperatives: strengthen the foundations (identity, least privilege, internet-facing exposure), secure AI systems as they enter the environment (treat AI agents' permissions and data access with the same rigor as human credentials), and deploy AI for defense at machine speed (continuous threat detection, AI-assisted triage, intelligence-to-action compression). Microsoft identified identity as the primary control plane — noting that 78% of attack techniques against critical infrastructure relied on cloud identity abuse.

What Does All of This Mean for Readers?

Most real-world intrusions still involve human direction for the highest-stakes decisions — target selection, complex operational choices. That caveat appears explicitly in the MDDR 2026: "Target selection, operational decision-making, and execution of the most complex intrusions remain manually driven in the majority of campaigns we observe." But Microsoft follows that sentence immediately with: the company expects those limits to fade.

JADEPUFFER already showed that autonomous extortion loops can operate in the wild. The 32-step enterprise compromise in a controlled evaluation showed that frontier models can chain together the full attack sequence without intervention. The question that the MDDR 2026 leaves open is not whether these capabilities will eventually be operationalized at scale — it is how quickly defenders can close the gap before they are.

The report's single most urgent recommendation: treat phishing-resistant multifactor authentication and passkeys not as a security upgrade but as a baseline requirement. Credential theft — enabled by phishing, password spraying, and infostealer markets — remains the dominant initial access vector. AI did not create that vulnerability. It made it cheaper and faster to exploit.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report find about AI and cyberattacks?

Microsoft's MDDR 2026 concluded that AI has already tipped the near-term advantage toward attackers. The report documented that the median window from vulnerability discovery to weaponization collapsed to under 24 hours, phishing as an attack vector nearly tripled as a share of intrusions (from 7% to 23% year-over-year), and the first fully autonomous ransomware extortion attack (JADEPUFFER) occurred in July 2026. Microsoft forecasts a multi-year period in which the backlog of known but unpatched vulnerabilities grows, because AI accelerates discovery faster than production systems can be safely patched. More detail is available in the full 2026 Digital Defense Report.

What is JADEPUFFER, and why does it matter?

JADEPUFFER, documented by the Sysdig Threat Research Team in July 2026, was the first confirmed case of a fully automated ransomware extortion attack — one in which AI-orchestrated systems autonomously handled the targeting, ransom demand delivery, and extortion workflow with minimal human direction. It matters because it crossed autonomous AI-enabled ransomware from a theoretical concern to a documented real-world event. Microsoft subsequently observed intrusions sharing JADEPUFFER characteristics at low volume, suggesting the operational model is being tested further. The JADEPUFFER attack mechanics were covered in detail by Help Net Security.

How are nation-state hackers using AI in attacks?

All four major state-sponsored threat clusters — China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran — have integrated AI into operational attack tradecraft, not just research. Chinese actors use AI to search for and iterate on exploits. Russian actors adopted "vibe coding" to rapidly generate attack tooling. North Korea's IT worker operations use AI deepfakes to pass job interviews, while separate DPRK groups use AI for malware creation, infrastructure management, and agentic attack workflows. Microsoft projects all four will expand autonomous AI use across the full intrusion lifecycle.

What can organizations do to defend against AI-powered cyberattacks?

Microsoft's MDDR 2026 identified three priorities: strengthen identity security (deploy phishing-resistant MFA and passkeys — credential theft remains the dominant initial access vector regardless of how it is obtained); accelerate patching for internet-facing systems (the sub-24-hour weaponization window means slow patch cycles are no longer viable for critical external vulnerabilities); and extend least-privilege controls to AI agents entering the environment, treating their permissions and data access with the same rigor applied to human user accounts. Organizations that deployed Microsoft Security Copilot reported summarizing threats 60 to 70% faster.

text:
Annie Lamont, co-founder and managing partner of Oak HC/FT, pointed out in an interview at the New York Stock Exchange that the reasons for numerous M&A failures are not complex: buyers acquire talent but then set these individuals aside outside of the decision-making framework after the deal closes.

She illustrated this with a comparison of investment banking mechanisms. After integrating teams, JPMorgan compares its own people with those from the acquired company to determine who is stronger, placing the stronger individuals in the corresponding positions without regard to their original organizational affiliations. In contrast, Credit Suisse prioritizes retaining existing employees' positions and does not place the globally strongest individuals from the acquired company in senior roles in lending, debt, and credit.

Lamont questioned the motivation behind such transactions: if a buyer acquires a globally top team in a certain capability but does not allow them to manage that business, the purchase itself loses its rationale. She distinguished between two cultures: one that adjusts positions to build a stronger company, and another that is politically motivated, aiming to maintain the status quo and expand territory.

The interview covered the backdrop of widening M&A activity in healthcare and fintech. Historically, the main buyers have been about five payers, along with distributors like McKesson and Cardinal, with healthcare institutions rarely making moves. She mentioned Microsoft's acquisition of healthcare-focused Nuance and Oracle's acquisition of Cerner, suggesting that frontier labs may further enter the healthcare asset space. She also stated that success depends on whether the buyer retains and utilizes talent or merely acquires products and data.

A positive example she provided was CareBridge's continued expansion after merging with Elevance. Oak HC/FT was founded by her and Andrew Adams in 2014, with public materials stating that it manages over $7 billion and has just completed a $2 billion sixth fund; she has over 40 years of personal investment experience, corresponding to over 70 exits, 15 IPOs, and seven entries into the Midas List. Her exit paths include One Medical's $3.9 billion sale to Amazon and CareBridge's $2.7 billion sale to Elevance.

This judgment points to the internal labor market post-acquisition, rather than the stock price on the announcement day. If the buyer only pays for consolidation, clients, or data, the original team sells out, and the budget and positions during the integration period still flow to the acquirer's old guard, leaving the acquired team without pricing power. The beneficiaries are the insiders who retain their positions, while the burden falls on the acquired business's client retention and revenue synergy. The event itself does not constitute a single-day capital flow but will change subsequent buyers' bids on "buying teams or buying assets."

Oak embeds talent search into the investment process rather than placing it in a post-closing human resources appendix. Its talent team recruited former Amazon supply chain executive Dave Clark, who initially leaned towards private equity acquisitions but later shifted to building the AI supply chain company Auger from scratch, with Oak committing $100 million on the first day. Under the same logic, she believes that companies lacking their strongest internal talent will be pushed towards being acquired rather than building that capability themselves.

Source: Public Information

Annie Lamont's approach is essentially "first buy capabilities, then decide who steers the ship." She participated in Apple's IPO roadshow in 1980, invested in athenahealth in 2000, and in 2014 spun off Oak HC/FT from Oak Investment Partners, focusing on healthcare and fintech. The exit list includes Aspire Health sold to Anthem, PayFlex sold to Aetna, VillageMD sold to Walgreens, One Medical sold to Amazon for $3.9 billion, and CareBridge sold to Elevance for $2.7 billion. The commonality among these transactions is not financial engineering but whether the acquired team can continue to manage the business within the buyer's system.

The flow of money follows the movement of people. Oak embeds talent functions into investment decisions rather than treating them as an appendix to post-closing human resources: the team first found Dave Clark and then shifted him from "buying a supply chain company" to building Auger from scratch, with a $100 million commitment on day one. Fund VI is about $2 billion, with individual checks ranging from $1 million to $100 million. The strategic motive is that in heavily regulated industries, if capabilities cannot be bought, they must be integrated. If the people brought in cannot occupy the corresponding positions, the check bought only reports, not capacity.

The comparison is not an abstract "culture" but two integration histories. JPMorgan has rearranged seats based on capabilities after multiple acquisitions, allowing transaction leaders like Anu Aiyengar to rise to global M&A heads from either the acquired or internal systems. Credit Suisse, after integrating teams like First Boston, has long maintained original organizational seating, leading to talent outflow in credit and leveraged finance, ultimately resulting in UBS taking over in 2023, with media teams and others moving to Evercore. The current situation is closer to a control phase rather than an expansion phase: healthcare buyers have expanded from five payers, McKesson, and Cardinal to Microsoft buying Nuance and Oracle buying Cerner, with more buyers emerging, but the integration power remains in the hands of the old guard.

This represents a transfer of pricing power, not a simple concentration of capital. The acquisition consideration buys the clients, credit, or clinical capabilities behind scarce positions. If positions are allocated according to original organizations post-closing, pricing power shifts from "acquired capabilities" back to "acquirer's political structure," and synergy revenue cannot be capitalized, leaving the selling founders to cash out and the buyer with only amortization. The failure rate is higher because transaction committees approve based on strategic narratives, and budgets and titles are allocated according to imperial logic, with two sets of books from day one not being the same transaction.

Buying a team but not giving them seats is equivalent to just buying a resume.

Acquisition consideration buys capabilities, while integration budgets buy insiders.

Seats allocated by origin means synergy stops at the announcement.
